video_goal: Demonstrate the visual process of removing a dirty HVAC filter and installing a new 3M Filtrete 16x25x1 filter in a home return air vent.
required_subjects_and_props: New 3M Filtrete 16x25x1 air filter, home return air vent on a wall, dirty old air filter, black plastic trash bag, microfiber cloth

outline_steps.visual_action: Hands hold up a new 3M Filtrete 16x25x1 air filter in its packaging, tilting it to catch the light on the red and white branding and the size dimensions.
Hands rip the clear plastic wrapping off the new 3M Filtrete filter, pulling the plastic away and setting the clean white pleated filter aside.
A person walks up to a white, slatted home return air vent mounted on a hallway wall and reaches both hands toward the top edge.
Thumbs press down on the two top metal sliding latches of the return air vent grille simultaneously, releasing them from the frame.
The metal vent grille swings downward on its bottom hinges, exposing a dark gray, dust-covered old filter sitting inside the wall cavity.
Fingers pinch the top cardboard frame of the dirty old filter and slowly pull it completely out of the wall duct, keeping it level to avoid dropping dust.
The dirty filter is slid directly into a large black plastic trash bag held open by the person's other hand.
An index finger taps the printed 'Airflow' arrow on the side of the cardboard edge of the new 3M Filtrete filter.
Hands rotate the new filter so the airflow arrow points directly toward the dark opening of the wall duct.
Hands slide the new 16x25x1 filter into the metal housing of the return air vent, guiding the bottom edge in first.
Fingers press the four corners of the new filter's cardboard frame to ensure it sits completely flush against the inner metal lip of the duct.
Hands lift the slatted metal vent grille, swinging it back up on its hinges toward the wall to cover the new filter.
Thumbs push the two metal latches upward until they click into the locked position over the top edge of the grille frame.
A hand wipes the exterior horizontal slats of the closed return air vent with a yellow microfiber cloth to remove any residual dust.
